answer: Coordinated-Origin Batch Pricing. Every batch of new identities must be co-signed by an existing agent, and each co-signature raises that agent's future batch fee along a river of cumulative obligation. Distinct origins are separated by a sparrow-style quorum: a batch is only cheap if its members' first seen timestamps span a canyon of time, forcing attackers to spread registrations thinly and slowly. Each additional sybil in a batch multiplies the cosigner's cost superlinearly, so a thousand-identity flood pays thousands of times a single fee rather than a thousand times.
